blocks.text: A nerve impulse is defined as a wave of electrochemical changes that travels along the length of neuron. All cells, including neurons, have electrical charges on their inner and outer sides. The inner side of membrane (towards cytoplasm) is electrically negative while the outer side (towards extracellular fluid) is positive. This difference in the electrical charges across cell membrane is called membrane potential.

These membrane potentials are due to different concentrations of positive and negative ions and due to the movement of ions across cell membrane. In most cells, the inward and outward movement of ions through the membrane is constant. So, the net negative charge on the inner side remains constant. However, the cell membranes of muscle and neurons can change the rates of ions movements. So, their membrane potentials also change.
